key_insight: Pretrained Vision Transformers can be augmented with a lightweight steering mechanism to redirect their attention toward user-specified or less-salient concepts while retaining their general-purpose visual features, enabling controllable visual representations without full model retraining.
problem_solved: Pretrained visual features typically focus on the most salient cues and lack a way to be directed toward less-prominent concepts; multimodal prompting shifts representations toward language and can lose visual fidelity, leaving a gap for controllable, visually faithful feature steering.
method: Add a lightweight steering module that conditions pretrained ViT features on guidance (textual prompts or visual exemplars) to reweight or modulate attention toward target concepts.
Train with objectives that balance amplifying target-concept responses and preserving the original, general-purpose feature space (e.g., contrastive/reconstruction regularization).
Apply steering at the feature level with minimal fine-tuning so the same backbone can be reused for multiple guided tasks (retrieval, fine-grained classification, segmentation).
impact: Provides practitioners a practical way to control off-the-shelf visual representations for task- or user-specific needs without expensive full-model fine-tuning, improving performance and interpretability on fine-grained or low-saliency tasks.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: pretrained ViT + steering module + guidance (text/image) → steered features → downstream task.
Before/after saliency or attention maps showing shift of focus from dominant cues to steered concepts.
Feature-space visualization (t-SNE/UMAP) comparing baseline vs. steered embeddings to show improved separation of target concepts.
Bar/line chart comparing downstream task metrics (retrieval, classification, segmentation) for baseline vs. steered representations.
paper_authors: Jona Ruthardt, Manu Gaur, Deva Ramanan, Makarand Tapaswi, Yuki M. Asano
